source_snapshot.procedure: Run `ipmitool sdr elist`, physically remove and insert the module, observe sensor status transitions and verify corresponding SEL records; source clears logs first.
source_snapshot.criteria: Temperature changes normally; settings including SDR type match SPEC; SEL records every threshold event; the system performs the specified threshold response such as fan-speed change or shutdown; both STATUS_CRPS1~2 pass.
source_snapshot.deepseek: NO correctly leaves physical CRPS service to an operator and limits the agent to status/SEL capture, but does not reconcile discrete module status with the thermal-threshold criteria or control live load transfer.
source_snapshot.gpt_v2: BLOCKED correctly identifies the status-versus-temperature mismatch and requires module mapping, redundancy and recovery. The conflict can be resolved by retaining independent CRPS status/load-transfer and thermal-threshold checkpoints rather than asking an engineer to choose one away.

old_problem: The historical record retained Pending, Source Conflict and BLOCKED because physical STATUS_CRPS1~2 presence transitions were judged by unrelated temperature-threshold language and no authoritative module/feed/event or safe service contract existed. The code is also reused at row 1521 for an AC-drop cycle, creating a false risk that evidence could be assigned to the wrong test identity.
disposition_reason: Preserve both source domains as mandatory but independent checkpoints. For CRPS1 and CRPS2, a qualified operator services exactly one mapped module at a time while read-only automation proves presence/status and SEL assert/deassert, measured load transfer to the survivor, stable output rails and return to full redundancy/load sharing. Separately, preserve the original temperature threshold, SEL and protective-response criteria through an approved thermal-sensor/fixture matrix; removal is never prolonged or repeated to manufacture a threshold. Row 1521 remains the independent AC-drop variant and supplies no evidence to this row. IPMI defines standard power-supply status offsets and sensor/SEL structure, while exact CRPS topology, event meanings, safe capacity, thermal oracle and recovery are finite Project inputs that gate execution rather than keep the engineering review Pending.
decision_basis: XLSX row 799, physical adjacent row 800, duplicate-code row 1521, exact same-row DeepSeek, exact GPT V2, tests JSON, selection manifest and historical V3.1 record were directly read. Row 800 / variant fd97aa9abcd81954 is the next formal queue case.

Duplicate Wistron-BMC-00089-V003 row 1521 / variant 2ea798d85e66e801 is Sanity BMC Cycle `AC drop 1 times`, with different procedure, criteria, script and duration. It cannot establish CRPS1/2 removal presence, per-module load transfer or reinsertion recovery and remains separately identifiable.

IPMI v2.0 sensor-specific type 08h defines Power Supply events including presence detected, failure, predictive failure, input lost, input lost/out-of-range and configuration error. Assertion/deassertion direction and event-data offset distinguish these states; removal presence must not be inferred from an AC-input-loss event.

IPMI Full/Compact SDR and Get Sensor Reading/Event Status define owner, sensor number, entity, type, masks and current state, while SEL records carry generator, sensor type/number, direction and event data. `ipmitool sdr elist` is a valid high-level read surface, but the target SDR and Project map remain the oracle for CRPS1 versus CRPS2 and OEM wording.

Removing one CRPS is simultaneously a physical presence change and a live power-topology change. A successful status transition without sufficient survivor capacity, stable rails and restored load sharing is not a safe or complete PASS.

Temperature remaining normal during a bounded service dwell is required safety/behavior evidence but cannot satisfy `sensor reach to each threshold`; those copied criteria therefore remain a separate controlled thermal checkpoint with their own sensor identities, thresholds, SEL and prescribed controller action.

ED-02 preserves duplicate source identity; ED-03 and ED-13 allow standard IPMI drafting but forbid guessed OEM mappings; ED-15 permits N/A only with authoritative applicability proof; ED-17 and ED-25 keep thermal fixtures and hardware service operator-controlled; ED-18 and ED-30 require approved thresholds; ED-19 preserves SEL before any mutation; ED-26 through ED-30 and ED-33 through ED-38 maintain independent coverage, confirmation, recovery and engineer verdict ownership.

test_case.test_name: CRPS1/2 presence, live load-transfer, SEL and independent thermal protection validation
test_case.purpose: Verify CRPS1 and CRPS2 independently change presence/status and log exact SEL events during approved removal/reinsertion, the surviving feed safely carries the measured load, full redundant load sharing recovers, and the original temperature-threshold/protection criteria pass as a separate controlled matrix without using AC drop or prolonged module removal as substitutes.
required_package: Immutable CRPS1/2 map: chassis slot, module model/serial/firmware, FRU/entity, latch, AC feed/PDU phase, PMBus address, STATUS_CRPS owner/LUN/number/ID, SDR/event type, normal/present/absent/fault states and raw SEL assertion/deassertion map

Vendor platform declaration for live CRPS removal/insertion or exact powered service state, connector/latch/feed order, dwell limit, same-module restoration and inspection; powered-down service must be labeled as not proving live failover

Project redundant-power contract: redundancy mode, feed topology, measured baseline demand, survivor rated and derated capacity, minimum headroom, load-transfer/share tolerance, output-rail limits, workload state, fan/thermal envelope and independent PDU/PMBus/rail telemetry

Pinned read-only evidence package: `ipmitool`, validated source-script revision or parser, BMC/SDR/chassis versions, complete SEL export/hash, CRPS/PMBus and host/OOB telemetry with correlated timestamps; no guessed raw write command

Independent thermal matrix retaining every applicable source threshold: exact temperature sensors, units/conversion, thresholds/hysteresis, SEL mapping, expected fan-speed/throttle/shutdown response, calibrated fixture profile, safe ceiling and recovery; unsupported points require SPEC-backed N/A
Per-module and per-thermal-action displayed approvals, trained operator, isolation window, abort owner and tested OOB recovery path
test_case.test_command: AUTHORIZED ATTENDED HYBRID PROCEDURE ONLY; DO NOT EXECUTE DURING REVIEW. Preserve/hash complete SEL and related logs; do not clear. Record immutable CRPS1/2 module/slot/serial/feed/SDR identities, input/output power, PMBus, rails, load share, redundancy, fan/temperature and host/BMC baseline. For CRPS1, then independently CRPS2: calculate and display current demand versus survivor derated capacity/headroom, exact service step, expected status/SEL/load transfer, dwell, aborts and recovery; obtain immediate approval. A qualified operator services only the named module using the vendor procedure. Read-only collection must prove the exact presence deassertion or mapped absent state, corresponding raw SEL assertion/deassertion direction, survivor load transfer and stable rails/host/thermal state. Reinsert and secure the same module once, restore its feed if the SOP requires, prove presence/status recovery, expected SEL recovery, stable share and full redundancy before the other module. Separately, with both CRPS modules restored, obtain a new approval and use only the authorized calibrated thermal fixture/profile to cross and re-arm each applicable temperature threshold; capture exact reading, event, SEL and prescribed fan/throttle/shutdown response plus recovery. Never substitute row-1521 AC drop, pull both modules, prolong removal to create heat, change thresholds/load-share controls, clear evidence, infer status from labels, retry an ambiguity or issue an automatic verdict.
test_case.expected_result: CRPS1 and CRPS2 each independently transition from the mapped present/normal state to the approved absent/degraded state and back, with exact raw SEL event direction/data, correct module/feed identity and no row-1521 AC-drop evidence. At each removal the survivor remains below its approved derated limit, output rails/host/BMC stay stable, redundancy changes exactly as specified and temperature remains inside the service envelope. Reinsertion restores FRU/status, input/output power, balanced sharing and full redundancy. Independently, every applicable mapped temperature threshold asserts/deasserts at its approved reading/hysteresis with the exact SEL and fan/throttle/shutdown behavior, then recovers.
test_case.pass_fail_basis: PASS requires both CRPS identities, two separately approved one-module service traces, exact status and raw SEL assertion/deassertion, measured safe load transfer, stable rails/host/BMC, bounded thermal behavior, same-module reinsertion and full load-share/redundancy recovery, plus the separately completed threshold/protection matrix. Static `sdr` output, operator statement alone, AC-input drop, aggregate power continuity, wrong event offset, missing deassertion, unmeasured survivor headroom, unexpected rail/redundancy/thermal behavior, powered-down replacement claimed as live failover, copied row-1521 evidence, missing threshold response, retry or incomplete recovery cannot pass. Missing packages are NOT READY; N/A requires authoritative Project/vendor proof and a platform defect is not N/A.
safety_gate: Never clear SEL or host/BMC logs. Export and hash the pre-action evidence and use timestamp markers; retain first-failure records before any recovery decision.

A trained operator alone handles CRPS modules, latches and feeds. Verify live-service support, exact serial/slot/feed, mechanical state and ESD requirements; automation performs only approved read-only observation and coordination.

Before each removal, prove measured workload plus margin fits the surviving module and feed under rated/derated Project limits; confirm OOB access and the exact immediate reinsertion or shutdown path.

Remove only one named CRPS. Abort and restore on wrong status/event, survivor overload/derating, rail excursion, unplanned redundancy loss, temperature/fan anomaly, unexpected input loss, host/BMC instability or mechanical uncertainty.
Thermal-threshold execution is separately approved and occurs only after both CRPS paths fully recover. Do not use an absent CRPS or altered fan/power policy as the heat source.
No automatic retry, AC cycle or power cycle. Preserve ambiguity/failure and let the power/thermal owner select recovery and any later controlled rerun.
expected_evidence: Exact Source Key/variant plus duplicate row-1521/variant exclusion; chassis, CRPS model/serial/firmware, slot/feed/PDU/PMBus/BMC/SDR/tool/script identities
Approved redundancy/load budget with measured demand, survivor derating/headroom, feed topology, service dwell, operator and recovery authorization for each module
Raw SDR/status and hashed SEL before/during/after each action, with generator/sensor/event direction/data decoded to the approved CRPS map
Time-aligned CRPS input/output, PMBus, PDU/feed, rails, load share, redundancy, fan/temperature, power-state and host/BMC telemetry for CRPS1 and CRPS2
Physical operator/photo evidence of the exact module removal, reinsertion, latch/feed restoration and final serial-bound configuration
Independent threshold/hysteresis matrix, calibrated thermal trace, raw sensor/SEL/controller response, full final recovery and per-checkpoint/overall engineer verdicts
test_case.recovery: On any service anomaly, do not touch the second module or repeat the action. Preserve telemetry/SEL, stop or reduce workload only through the approved owner plan, reinsert and secure the exact module when safe, restore its feed, and verify presence/status, PMBus, rails, share, redundancy, fans, temperatures, BMC and host. If the survivor overloads, rails destabilize, the module cannot be restored or OOB visibility is lost, follow the pre-approved controlled shutdown/isolation procedure and escalate; no implicit AC or power cycle is authorized. On a thermal-fixture anomaly, stop the stimulus, restore cooling/environment and follow the thermal owner. Retain first-failure evidence and require a new authorization before any later rerun.

source_conflict.reason: The Review layer retains CRPS presence/load-transfer and temperature-threshold/protection as separate mandatory checkpoints, so neither signal is selected away. The duplicate AC-drop row remains excluded by Source Key, physical row and Variant ID.

blocked.reason: Standard IPMI power-supply event semantics support a correct generic contract, and safe service/load-transfer/thermal checkpoints are fully specified. Target module/feed mapping, survivor capacity, OEM event oracle and thresholds are finite Project packages that gate execution as NOT READY rather than an unresolved engineering choice.

pending.remaining_project_configuration: CRPS1/2 serial-slot-feed-PMBus-SDR-SEL map; vendor live-service capability/SOP; redundancy/load/derating/rail/thermal limits; independent threshold/response/fixture matrix; OOB recovery, evidence and approval owners.
pending.execution_status: NOT STARTED; REVIEW-LAYER HYBRID CASE ONLY; NO CRPS, AC, SENSOR, THERMAL, SEL, LOG, IPMI, POWER OR DUT ACTION EXECUTED

external_authorities.title: Intelligent Platform Management Interface Specification v2.0 rev. 1.1
external_authorities.application: Power Supply sensor type 08h defines presence, failure, predictive failure, input-loss/out-of-range and configuration-error offsets; sensor/SDR/SEL sections define identity, state, assertion/deassertion direction and raw event correlation. Platform/OEM mapping and safe power capacity are not inferred from the standard.

project_authority: The Project power, platform, BMC and thermal owners approve the CRPS serial/slot/feed/status map, live-service support, measured survivor capacity, load/rail/thermal limits, threshold/controller oracle, operator steps and OOB recovery. They own per-module, thermal and overall verdicts; confirmation cannot make AC-drop evidence, missing load telemetry, guessed event data, powered-down-only service or an unexecuted threshold PASS.
